triples.relationship: Ceremonial comparison: a leader on a raised structure before the assembly
triples.rationale: Esdras stands on a wooden platform during the public reading of the law. Solomon stands and then kneels on a bronze base of stated height opposite Israel's assembly for prayer. Both place the leader on a constructed raised support in communal worship; the materials, actions and ceremonies differ, and the attendants beside Esdras are not identified through Solomon's ceremony.
triples.source_text: Esdras the scribe stood on a wooden platform. Beside him stood Mattathias, Samaias, Ananias, Ouria, Elkia and Maasaia on his right, and on his left Phadaias, Misael, Melchias, Osam, Asabdana, Zacharias and Mosollam.

target_units.text: For Solomon had made a bronze base and put it in the middle of the temple court, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high. He stood on it, fell on his knees opposite all Israel’s assembly, and spread out his hands toward heaven.

triples.relationship: Liturgical parallel: Levites stand and address God with a loud voice
triples.rationale: The named Levites stand on their ascent and cry loudly to the Lord in the assembled people's confession and worship. In Chronicles, after the assembly bows, Levites stand to praise the Lord with a loud voice raised high. Both give Levites a prominent standing and vocal role in communal worship, without equating the named groups or the occasions.
triples.source_text: Jesus and the sons of Kadmiel, Sachania son of Sarabia, the sons of Chanani, stood on the Levites’ ascent and cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God.

target_units.text: Jehoshaphat bowed on his face, and all Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants fell before the Lord to worship the Lord.
The Levites from the sons of Kaath and the sons of Kore stood up to praise the Lord, the God of Israel, with a loud voice raised high.

triples.relationship: Ritual parallel: ministers purified before performing purification
triples.rationale: At the wall dedication, the priests and Levites are purified and then purify the people, gatekeepers and wall. In Hezekiah's cleansing, the Levites first purify themselves, and priests and Levites then cleanse the Lord's house. The shared sequence joins the ministers' own purification to their work of purification; Nehemiah's unstated rite and source of uncleanness are not supplied from Chronicles.
triples.source_text: The priests and Levites were purified, and they purified the people, the gatekeepers and the wall.

target_units.text: They gathered their brethren and purified themselves according to the king’s command, through the Lord’s ordinance, to cleanse the Lord’s house.

The priests went inside the Lord’s house to purify it. They cast out all the uncleanness found in the Lord’s house into the courtyard of the Lord’s house, and the Levites received it to cast it outside into the Kedron torrent.

triples.relationship: Linguistic comparison: Judean speech and its audience
triples.rationale: Nehemiah distinguishes children who speak Azotian but cannot speak Judean. The Jerusalem officials in Kings distinguish Syrian, which they understand, from Judean, which the envoy uses within the people's hearing. The comparison establishes the texts' use of Judean as a community language and highlights differing language competence; Azotian is not equated with Syrian, and no conclusion about the children's knowledge of the law is added.
triples.source_text: and half their children spoke Azotian and did not know how to speak Judean.

target_units.text: Eliakim son of Chelkias, Somnas, and Joash said to Rhapsakes, ‘Please speak to your servants in Syrian, for we understand it. Do not speak with us in Judean. Why are you speaking within the hearing of the people on the wall?’

Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, who are to eat their own dung and drink their own urine together with you?’
Rhapsakes stood and cried out loudly in Judean: ‘Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians!
